messages.subject: left_join by range
messages.body_plain:

I'm trying to join two tables by taking a numeric value in one column and finding it's matching range (based on two columns) in the other data frame. Here's a toy example:

first_df <-
  data_frame(
    start_time = c(20, 30, 40),
    end_time = c(29, 39, 49)
  )

second_df <-
  data_frame(
    arrival_time = c(25, 33, 47),
    person = c("Bob", "Robert", "Rob")
  )

# doesn't work; just shows the logic I'm looking for
left_join(first_df, second_df, by = c("start_time" < "arrival_time" & "end_time" > "arrival_time"))

I'd like to end up with a data frame like this:
  start_time end_time person
1         20       29     Bob
2         30       39     Robert
3         40       49     Rob

While I can use several for loops to get the result, I'm wondering if there is a less painful way, possibly with left_join().

Thanks for your any ideas.

> f2

manipulatr-ers,

Within a function, I'm trying to exclude rows with NAs in one column using dplyr::filter, but leave in rows that may have NAs in other columns (therefore, I can't pipe the data frame through na.omit). The column name is given by the user of the function. Here's a toy example:

library("dplyr")
library("lazyeval")

df <- data_frame(
  dept = c("marketing", "marketing", "marketing", "accounting", "accounting"),
  person = c("Bob", "Bill", "Rich", "Stan", "Fred"),
  age = c(23, 34, NA, 45, NA),
  salary = c(8000, NA, 10000, NA, 20000)
)

## begin function definition ##
get_info <- function(df.name <http://df.name>, dept.name <http://dept.name>, col.name <http://col.name>) {
  output <-
    df.name <http://df.name> %>%
    filter(dept == dept.name <http://dept.name>) %>%

    # TRYING TO EXCLUDE NAs IN THE COLUMN SPECIFIED BY THE USER
    filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(col.name <http://col.name>))
#     filter_(!is.na <http://is.na>(~col.name <http://col.name>))
#     filter_(!is.na <http://is.na>(interp(quote(var.name <http://var.name>), var.name <http://var.name> = col.name <http://col.name>)))
#     filter_(!is.na <http://is.na>(~interp(col.name <http://col.name>)))
#     filter_(!is.na <http://is.na>(~interp(var.name <http://var.name>, var.name <http://var.name> = col.name <http://col.name>)))

  return(output)
}
## end function definition ##

# tests the function
get_info(df, "marketing", "age")

2 marketing   Bill  34     NA

Rather than the desired:

2 marketing   Bill  34     NA

messages.body_plain:
I suppose this is mostly for Hadley, Romain, etc, but I wanted to post it here to get any further comments, and I don't think these are
specific enough for pull requests:

1) I've never been sure why you'd use select instead of transmute.  I think it would be simpler to just rename transmute into select.

2) I think this may have been requested before, but it would be _very_ handy to have something like

mutate_filter( filter expression, mutate expression) that mutates records that satisfy a filter condition.

It would be equivalent (in loose sql) to update tbl set <mutate expressions> where <filter expression>.
I realize you need to set any new columns to NA for rows which do not satisfy the filter and that you can do the same thing with
the idiom
rbind(filter(dt,!condition),filter(dt,condition) %>% mutate), but that's pretty ugly for such a simple thing, and it doens't
preserve previous "arrange" operations.

2a)  I've gotten around this in the past using rowwise %>% mutate(value=ifelse(condition,newvalue,value)) but I don't know how
to "unrowwise" without going back to a dataframe.  That idiom still is uglier than the suggestion above.

3) Along those lines, it would be nice to be able to update dataframes in joins, e.g.

left_join(dta,dtb,update=T) which take dtb's values iff they match in dta.

Again, could be done with rbinds, or using data.table's' syntax rbindlist(list(a[!b],b),use.names=TRUE,fill=FALSE), but I think
amending left_join would be a lot cleaner.

If I'm missing a nifty way to do these operations, please let me know!
